indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.sub_strand: Data Collection, Organization, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis
indicator.content_standard: Select, justify, and use appropriate methods of collecting data, including questionnaires, interview, observation, experiments, databases, electronic media, etc.
indicator.objective: Design and administer a questionnaire for collecting data to answer given question(s), record the data, analyse and graph the results to solve problems

skills.description: Organise tallies into a frequency table.
Draw a bar or line graph from frequency data.

questions.stem: Which is the best survey question to find the favourite drink of pupils in a class?
options: Do you drink Fanta or Coke?
hints: A good question is open and clear.
It should not suggest an answer.
questions.explanation: 'What is your favourite drink?' is clear and does not lead the respondent.
questions.misconception: Choosing 'Do you like Fanta?', which is a yes/no question that favours one drink.

questions.stem: Which is the best survey question to find out how pupils travel to school?
options: How do you travel to school?
Why do you take a trotro?
Do you walk or take a trotro?
hints: A good question allows many possible answers.
It should not limit choices to two.
questions.explanation: 'How do you travel to school?' allows all forms of transport to be reported.
questions.misconception: Choosing 'Do you walk or take a trotro?', which ignores other transport.

questions.stem: A pupil wants to know the favourite subject of each classmate. Which question is best?
options: Do you like Maths or English?
Why is Maths your favourite subject?
hints: A good question is open to all subjects.
It should not assume a subject.
questions.explanation: 'What is your favourite subject?' is clear and open.
questions.misconception: Choosing 'Why is Maths your favourite subject?', which assumes Maths is the favourite.

questions.stem: What is wrong with the survey question: 'Do you agree that Fanta is the best drink?'
options: It leads the respondent to agree
questions.explanation: The question is leading because it suggests Fanta is the best.
questions.misconception: Thinking the question is fine because it mentions a popular drink.

questions.stem: A pupil asks: 'Do you walk or take a trotro to school?' What is the problem with this question?
options: It is double-barrelled and leaves out other options
It is not a survey question
hints: Some pupils may cycle or be driven.
The question limits answers to two options.
questions.explanation: The question only allows two answers and ignores other ways of travelling.
questions.misconception: Thinking two options are always enough.

questions.stem: A pupil asks: 'How many minutes do you spend on homework and what is your favourite subject?' What is wrong?
options: It is double-barrelled (asks two questions in one)
hints: Count how many things are being asked.
A respondent can only answer one part.
questions.explanation: The question asks two different things, making it double-barrelled.
questions.misconception: Thinking combining questions saves time.

questions.stem: Write one clear survey question to find out how many hours per week pupils spend reading at home.

criteria.description: The question is clear and not leading
The question asks about hours per week and reading at home

hints: Include 'hours per week' and 'reading at home'.
questions.explanation: Example: 'How many hours per week do you spend reading at home?'
questions.misconception: Writing 'Do you read a lot at home?', which is vague.

questions.stem: A tally chart shows: Fanta |||| (5), Coke ||| (3), Sprite || (2). How many pupils chose Fanta?
hints: Count the tally marks for Fanta.
questions.explanation: Fanta has 5 tallies, so 5 pupils chose it.
questions.misconception: Adding all tallies to get 10.

questions.stem: Tallies: Maths |||| (5), English ||| (3), Science || (2). What is the total number of pupils surveyed?
questions.misconception: Counting only the first category.

questions.stem: A frequency table shows: Walk 8, Trotro 12, Car 4. How many pupils travel by trotro?
questions.misconception: Adding all rows to get 24.

questions.stem: Tally chart: Red |||| || (7), Blue |||| (5), Green ||| (3). Which colour has the highest frequency?
questions.misconception: Choosing Blue because it is a common colour.

questions.stem: A frequency table shows: Football 15, Athletics 10, Basketball 5. What fraction of pupils chose Football?
questions.misconception: Using only the other categories to find the denominator.

questions.stem: A frequency table shows: Boys 18, Girls 12. What is the ratio of boys to girls in simplest form?
questions.misconception: Writing 2:3 by reversing.

questions.stem: A tally chart shows: Fanta |||| (5), Coke ||| (3), Sprite || (2). Complete a frequency table and explain how you would use it to draw a bar graph.

criteria.description: Explains that the x-axis shows drinks and the y-axis shows frequency

hints: List each drink and its count.
The bar height equals the frequency.
questions.explanation: Frequency table: Fanta 5, Coke 3, Sprite 2. Draw bars of heights 5, 3, 2 above each drink.
questions.misconception: Swapping the axes.

questions.stem: A frequency table shows: Maths 6, English 4, Science 5. Which type of graph is best to display this data?
questions.explanation: A bar graph is best for comparing categories.
questions.misconception: Choosing a line graph, which suggests continuity.

questions.stem: A bar graph shows Fanta 5, Coke 3, Sprite 2. Which drink has the lowest bar?
questions.misconception: Choosing Coke because it is a well-known brand.

questions.stem: A pupil draws a bar graph of favourite subjects with bars Maths 6, English 4, Science 5. What should the y-axis be labelled?
questions.explanation: The y-axis should show 'Number of pupils'.
questions.misconception: Labelling the y-axis with subject names.

questions.stem: A bar graph shows 8 pupils walk, 12 take a trotro, 4 come by car. How many pupils were surveyed in total?
questions.misconception: Reading only the tallest bar.

questions.stem: A bar graph shows: Football 15, Athletics 10, Basketball 5. What conclusion can you draw?
options: Football is the most popular sport
hints: The tallest bar shows the most popular.
questions.explanation: Football has the highest bar, so it is the most popular.
questions.misconception: Choosing Basketball because it is well-known.

questions.stem: A pupil draws a bar graph with unequal gaps between bars and no title. What two improvements should be made?
options: Equal gaps between bars and add a title
Add more bars and a key
Change colours and add a title
Use a line graph and add a title
questions.explanation: Use equal gaps between bars and add a clear title.
questions.misconception: Thinking colours matter more than equal spacing.
